thread.title: UPDATE: How BlackBerry's 'beast' of a breakout makes the stock a beauty to hold again

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: How BlackBerry's 'beast' of a breakout makes the stock a beauty to hold again
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
This cold jobs-day morning has stocks skating toward a weekly win, with the Dow apparently feeling pretty snug above 25,000.
"We are certainly seeing an overheated market," says technical analyst Mark Arbeter (https://twitter.com/MarkArbeter). "Too bad we can't borrow some of that heat for our homes this winter."
The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 has been this holiday-shortened week's "bomb cyclone" among the stock indexes, exploding for a weekly gain of 2.9%, ahead of the Dow's 1.4% rise.
Even somewhat forsaken tech stocks have soared, such as BlackBerry (BB.T) (BB.T) , which was kicked out (http://business.inquirer.net/98425/blackberry-maker-dropped-from-nasdaq-100) of the Nasdaq-100 (QQQ) years ago.
Shares in the Canadian company -- now focused on software (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/at-blackberry-smartphones-play-decreasing-role-2015-05-19) after becoming a smartphone also-ran -- have jumped 20% for the week as of yesterday's close, touching levels last seen in 2013.
"BlackBerry has a lot of potential to run, and if you're playing this long term, then I would definitely be looking to hold this," says ChartYourTrade.com founder Michael Lamothe (https://twitter.com/MichaelGLamothe/status/948660426438533120) for our call of the day.
The stock has been "a beast" lately, and it has shown it can attract buyers around its 40-week moving average, Lamothe says. That chart level is shown in graphic below.
This week's leap is being pinned on BlackBerry's deal with Baidu (BIDU) -- the Google of China -- that calls for the two companies to work together on self-driving car technology. It follows other BlackBerry pacts related to autonomous vehicles, including ones with chip giant Qualcomm (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-blackberry-baidu/blackberry-surges-on-deal-with-baidu-for-self-driving-cars-idUSKBN1ES15V)(QCOM) and auto supplier Delphi (https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-autos-selfdriving/delphi-blackberry-partner-on-self-driving-software-system-idUKKCN1BV2CO)(DLPH) .
Read:After driverless cars, BlackBerry aims at trucks to reach profit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/after-driverless-cars-blackberry-aims-at-trucks-to-reach-profit-2016-03-31)
For shorter-term traders, Lamothe advises selling into the recent strength. He has been doing exactly that, as he had planned to make BlackBerry a quick swing trade, he says.
Also among those juiced about BlackBerry is financial blogger and trader ChessNwine.
"This is going to be the real test: Can BlackBerry make a meaningful higher low now above this $12-$13 area?" he says (https://marketchess.com/2018/01/04/stock-market-recap-01-04-18-video). That is a "big, big level long term." (Chart watchers often look for higher lows, as they can signal (https://www.investopedia.com/terms/r/reversal.asp) a downtrend has flipped into an uptrend.)
For his part, BlackBerry CEO John Chen has been declaring that his company is baa-aaack -- or in his words, "not in a turnaround mode anymore (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-01-03/blackberry-baidu-partner-to-work-on-driverless-car-software)."
Key market gauges
Futures for the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 are moving up, after the Dow , S&P and Nasdaq Composite all scored all-time closing highs yesterday, with the Dow topping 25K for the first time (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-on-track-for-25000-milestone-as-global-stock-rally-stays-strong-2018-01-04).
European (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-for-3rd-day-as-global-rally-stays-strong-2018-01-05) and Asian stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-continue-soaring-to-new-highs-but-show-signs-of-cooling-2018-01-04) have gained. Oil (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-fall-losing-grip-on-3-year-high-2018-01-05) is retreating as the dollar (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-rebounds-as-traders-look-to-jobs-data-for-inflation-hints-2018-01-05) rises. Gold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/golds-long-win-streak-hits-pause-ahead-of-jobs-report-2018-01-05) is little changed.
On the cryptocurrencies front, Ripple coins have been dropping (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bitcoin-rises-as-ripples-surge-pauses-after-exchange-says-its-not-adding-the-assets-yet-2018-01-05) after crypto exchange Coinbase gave them the cold shoulder, while bitcoin has been advancing.
See the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sp-eyes-another-historic-record-run-with-us-jobs-data-on-deck-2018-01-05) for the latest action.
The chart
All the tax-reform hype might be overdone, suggests Deutsche Bank economist Torsten Slok, who offers the chart above. It shows where the latest planned tax cut ranks as a percentage of GDP, revealing it's below what we got in 2010 and 2013.
The buzz
(https://twitter.com/bySamRo/status/949063679877709824)
As Sears Holdings (SHLD)closes 64 Kmarts and 39 Sears locations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sears-to-close-more-than-100-stores-including-kmart-locations-in-march-and-april-2018-01-04), the handy UBS chart above shows which retailers shuttered the most U.S. stores last year.
While it has been a nice week for BlackBerry -- blown out of the water by the iPhone years ago -- Apple (AAPL) is scrambling to safeguard its gadgets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-admits-its-devices-are-affected-by-meltdown-and-spectre-chip-bugs-2018-01-04) from the Meltdown and Spectre chip bugs.
The December reading on nonfarm payrolls hit before the open, showing the U.S. added fewer jobs than expected. Wage growth is getting described as "disappointing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-148000-jobs-in-december-2018-01-05)."
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
Mark Zuckerberg plans on "fixing" Facebook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mark-zuckerbergs-new-year-resolution-fix-facebook-2018-01-05)(FB) this year.
Corona beer parent Constellation Brands (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/corona-beer-distributor-constellation-brands-sales-falls-short-of-estimates-2018-01-05)(STZ) is among the companies that has posted earnings before the open.
A pre-Olympics thaw? North and South Korea plan to hold high-level talks Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/north-korea-agrees-to-high-level-talks-with-south-korea-next-week-2018-01-04).
Is Ripple's co-founder becoming the world's richest man (https://www.inverse.com/article/39938-ripple-cryptocurrency-chris-larsen-net-worth)? Maybe not (http://www.valuewalk.com/2018/01/ripple-co-founder-chris-larsen-richest-man-world/).
Cryptocurrencies and the blockchain technology underlying them could become a $10 trillion market in 15 years, says an RBC analyst (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/01/03/one-stock-analysts-10-trillion-bull-case-for-cryptocurrencies.html).
The Trump administration is seeking $18 billion for new barriers (https://www.wsj.com/articles/trump-administration-seeks-18-billion-over-decade-to-expand-border-wall-1515148381) along our border with Mexico, offering the most detailed description yet of the president's planned wall.
